item.title: King Frederik arrived at Nuuk Airport in Greenland
item.description: King Frederik arrived in Greenland on Wednesday for a three-day visit. He was welcomed at Nuuk Airport by government leader Jens-Frederik Nielsen and Parliament Chairman Kim Kielsen. item.title: How to prepare for and what to expect from your job interview in Denmark
item.description: Danish interviews value preparation, authenticity, and dialogue over formality. Jobindex’s Head of Employment explains how internationals can navigate expectations, avoid common mistakes, and present themselves effectively to employers.

item.title: Enhedslisten wants to tax housing gains over one million DKK at 15%
item.description: Pelle Dragsted, political leader of Enhedslisten, has proposed a 15 percent tax on housing gains exceeding one million DKK. He argues it is “fundamentally unfair” that labor is taxed heavily while multi-million property gains in Copenhagen remain largely tax-free. The proposal is expected to generate two billion DKK in revenue. Half would be used to […]

item.title: Canadian ambassador to Denmark: “We were over-reliant on the US. Now we must be self-reliant, and work with like-minded neighbors and friends”
item.description: The Copenhagen Post interviewed Carolyn Bennett a few days after Canada opened an embassy in Greenland: "The neighborhood may not be as friendly as it once was, and we all have to stick together in the North in terms of Arctic security and defense," she explains.

item.title: Greenlandic recruits show diving gear to the King
item.description: King Frederik met 18 students from the Arctic Basic Education program in Nuuk on Wednesday. This six-month military course in Kangerlussuaq is exclusive to Greenland residents and provides skills for the Danish Defence and local emergency services. In front of the inspection ship “Vædderen,” students demonstrated diving equipment and discussed their motivations with the King. […]

item.title: North Jutland ammo plant 480m more than planned
item.description: The ammunition factory in Elling, North Jutland, will be approximately 480 million DKK more expensive than anticipated, according to the Ministry of Defence. The additional costs are attributed to larger building areas necessitated by detonation risks, infrastructure adjustments, and an extra shooting range. item.title: Social Democrats: Build new homes instead of taxing
item.description: The Social Democratic party has definitively rejected changing current housing taxes or introducing a tax on housing gains. item.title: Summer house buyers undeterred by snow and cold
item.description: The Danish holiday home market has been remarkably active since the start of the year, despite wintry conditions. In January, 613 holiday homes were sold nationwide, a nine percent increase from last year. Boligsiden economist Birgit Daetz notes that interest now spans the entire year. item.title: Hundreds at kaffemik with King Frederik in Nuuk
item.description: King Frederik joined hundreds of people for a traditional kaffemik—a Greenlandic gathering with coffee and pastries—at the Katuaq cultural center in Nuuk on Wednesday. item.title: LA wants European nuclear weapons in Denmark.
item.description: Liberal Alliance chairman Alex Vanopslagh states that Denmark should be willing to invest in nuclear weapons and allow their storage on Danish soil. To support a European nuclear umbrella, the party proposes lifting Denmark’s 70-year-old ban on nuclear weapons.
